    Finite Stern–Brocot plane test and silting count in rank two #

    Proposition 8.3 (cor:stern-brocot) of the manuscript. For an algebra of rank two with indecomposable projectives P, Q and x = dim_k Hom(Q, P), y = dim_k Hom(P, Q), the g-vector fan covers the entire plane if and only if the finitely many Stern–Brocot mediants of depths x and y in the two mixed quadrants lie in Σ(R), in which case there are at most 2^x + 2^y + 2 basic two-term silting complexes (sternBrocot_plane_test_and_count).

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.plane_covered_iff_projective_mediants (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (P Q : FiniteProjective R) (hPQ : ∀ (T : FiniteProjective R), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable ↑T → Nonempty (↑T ≅ ↑P) ∨ Nonempty (↑T ≅ ↑Q)) :
    (∀ (v : RealProjectiveSpace R), ∃ (E : TwoTerm R) (L : TwoTerm R), (E.directSum L).IsPresilting ∧ v ∈ sectorBetween ((realProjectiveClass R) E.projectiveClass) ((realProjectiveClass R) L.projectiveClass)) ↔ ProjectiveMediantsCovered k P Q

    A pair representing every indecomposable projective gives the plane criterion. The depth in each mixed quadrant is the corresponding Hom dimension.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.fan_covers_plane_iff_projective_mediants (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (P Q : FiniteProjective R) (hPQ : ∀ (T : FiniteProjective R), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable ↑T → Nonempty (↑T ≅ ↑P) ∨ Nonempty (↑T ≅ ↑Q)) :
    (∀ (v : RealProjectiveSpace R), ∃ (T : TwoTerm R), T.IsPresilting ∧ v ∈ T.gVectorCone) ↔ ProjectiveMediantsCovered k P Q

    The support of the g-vector fan is the whole real plane exactly when the finitely many mixed-quadrant mediants have presilting representatives.

        For the two projective directions in rank two, membership of the finitely many mediants in the fan is equivalent to coverage of the whole plane. Under this test the number of basic two-term silting complexes is at most 2^x + 2^y + 2.
